title: Image Classification, Object Detection and OCR
summary: Distinguish image classification, object detection and OCR by what each one actually outputs, and try each on a sample image.
objectives: Send a POST request with a JSON body to the practice API
Read a label, a list of boxes and extracted text out of JSON responses
Tell classification, detection and OCR apart by their outputs
Write a short comparison of what each tool returned

segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

Classification, object detection and OCR are three different tools that answer three different questions. In this lab you send the same photo, `street_sign.png`, to the practice API three times: `POST /vision/classify` gives one label for the whole image, `POST /vision/detect` gives a list of labelled boxes with coordinates, and `POST /ocr` reads the text on the shop sign. The API is simulated inside the lab and answers from a fixed table, so it only needs the image's file name. You print the top label, the number of boxes and the text, then write a comparison of at least 30 words in a variable called `write_up`: what each tool returned and where it was right or wrong.

lab.title: One photo, three tools
lab.objective: Run a classifier, an object detector and OCR on the same photo through the practice API, and compare what each one returned.
lab.instructions:
The photo street_sign.png (a street with a shop sign, a parked car and a person) is in your working directory. The practice API at https://api.neuromind.lab/v1 knows this photo by its file name: every request is a POST with json={"image": "street_sign.png"}.

1. Print Image file: street_sign.png and its size in bytes with os.path.getsize(IMAGE).
2. Classification: POST to /vision/classify. The answer is {"labels": [{"label": ..., "score": ...}, ...]}, best first. Store the list in labels, the first label's text in top_label, and print Top label: followed by it.
3. Detection: POST to /vision/detect. The answer is {"objects": [{"label": ..., "box": [x1, y1, x2, y2], "score": ...}, ...]}. Store the list in objects and len(objects) in box_count. Print Boxes: followed by box_count, then one line per object with its label and box.
4. OCR: POST to /ocr. The answer is {"text": ..., "lines": [...]}. Store the text in ocr_text, print OCR text: and then the text itself.
5. Write a comparison of at least 30 words in a string called write_up. Name all three tools (classifier, detector, OCR), say what each one returned (one label, boxes with coordinates, or text) and whether it was right or wrong for this photo. Print it after Write-up:.

Expected lines in your output:
Top label: street
Boxes: 3
OCR text:
RAO & SONS BAKERY
OPEN 7 AM - 9 PM
lab.constraints: Use requests.post() with json={"image": IMAGE} for every call. Only https://api.neuromind.lab/v1 is reachable. Read every value from response.json(); do not type the answers in. Keep the names labels, top_label, objects, box_count, ocr_text and write_up. No input().

import os
import requests

BASE = "https://api.neuromind.lab/v1"
IMAGE = "street_sign.png"   # the photo is in your working directory; the API knows it by this name

# 1. Print "Image file:", IMAGE and its size in bytes (os.path.getsize(IMAGE)) so you know the file is there.


# 2. Classification: POST to BASE + "/vision/classify" with json={"image": IMAGE}.
#    labels = response.json()["labels"]  (a list of {"label", "score"} dicts, best first)
#    top_label = the "label" of the first one. Print "Top label:" followed by top_label.


# 3. Detection: POST to BASE + "/vision/detect" with the same JSON body.
#    objects = response.json()["objects"]; box_count = len(objects).
#    Print "Boxes:" followed by box_count, then one line per object with its label and box.


# 4. OCR: POST to BASE + "/ocr" with the same JSON body.
#    ocr_text = response.json()["text"]. Print "OCR text:" and then ocr_text on the next line.


# 5. Compare the three results in your own words (at least 30 words) in a string called write_up.
#    Name all three tools (classifier, detector, OCR) and say what each returned and whether it was right or wrong.
write_up = ""
print("Write-up:", write_up)
hints: All three calls look the same: response = requests.post(BASE + "/vision/classify", json={"image": IMAGE}) and then data = response.json(). Only the path changes: /vision/classify, /vision/detect, /ocr.

The classifier's answer is data["labels"], a list of dictionaries, so the best label is data["labels"][0]["label"]. The detector's answer is data["objects"]; its length is the number of boxes. OCR gives data["text"].

For write_up, use three sentences: 'The classifier returned ...', 'The detector returned ... boxes ...', 'OCR read the text ...'. Say whether each one was right. Count the words: you need at least 30.

lab.solution:
import os
import requests

BASE = "https://api.neuromind.lab/v1"
IMAGE = "street_sign.png"

print("Image file:", IMAGE, "(" + str(os.path.getsize(IMAGE)) + " bytes)")

response = requests.post(BASE + "/vision/classify", json={"image": IMAGE})
labels = response.json()["labels"]
top_label = labels[0]["label"]
print("Top label:", top_label)

response = requests.post(BASE + "/vision/detect", json={"image": IMAGE})
objects = response.json()["objects"]
box_count = len(objects)
print("Boxes:", box_count)
for obj in objects:
    print(" -", obj["label"], obj["box"])

response = requests.post(BASE + "/ocr", json={"image": IMAGE})
ocr_text = response.json()["text"]
print("OCR text:")
print(ocr_text)

write_up = (
    "The classifier returned one label for the whole photo, street, which is right but says nothing about where things are. "
    "The detector returned three boxes for a car, a person and a sign with coordinates, so it is the right tool for finding objects. "
    "OCR ignored the objects and read the text on the sign, RAO & SONS BAKERY and the opening hours, which neither of the other tools could do."
)
print("Write-up:", write_up)
